## A. Exact inherited BRC interface and new clock question

Input: research_notes/chatgpt_direct/20261010_EULER_PASSIVE_SAMPLING_AND_NOISE.md, immutable proof commit 0b0f5d9df0e079d23746bf3334f7888cf661b641; proof blob bd80290c259cc60995069613a5f4b5f41a13d1; SHA256 15b59435bfd72496a8eee1b7c5b9eaf57090cda6099b2ebac86dfb554558e1b7. Its current checkpoint and full proof were read. The source is PROVISIONAL, not an independently admitted theorem.

The source retains twelve positive paths, each weight 1/12, one fixed conserved Q sector, their joint fields and phases, and the preset BRC command word T=H03,U2,C. Its exact continuing-family observer law is:

    Z(k)=1/4 if k=11 mod 12; Z(k)=0 otherwise.

Its zero comparator has the same positive accounting and Z(k)=0 for every k. This turn consumes that exact law as a hypothesis. It neither reconstructs world dynamics from scalar values nor reruns the 384-atom controller. k is a whole command-word round, not physical time.

The new observer reads Y(n)=Z(k_n), with integer round labels k_n. No measurement disturbance is assumed. This is an explicit adversarial observation-clock class, not a claim that a physical/native incident clock realizes it.

### A1. One-round bounded skew plus repeated samples can hide the pulse forever

For every n>=0 set

    k_n=n+1 if n=11 mod 12, and k_n=n otherwise.

Then k_0=0, 0<=k_n-n<=1, and each increment is 0, 1 or 2. The observation is monotone but may repeat a round. Its image omits every integer equal to 11 mod12: at nominal residue11 it jumps to residue0, and the following sample repeats that same round. Consequently Y(n)=0 for all n, even though Z(11+12r)=1/4 for every r>=0.

Thus an infinite sequence of zero samples cannot separate this positive preparation from the existing zero comparator under this clock class. This is a structural sampling obstruction under the inherited BRC observer; it is not roundoff, loss of positive mass, measurement backreaction, or proof of any physical residual. The all-n construction proves the obstruction; the finite scan only checks it.

### A2. Strictly increasing samples with a bounded skip budget: exact deadline

Generalize to any period L>=2 with a pulse at L-1 modL. Assume k_0=0, k_(n+1)>=k_n+1, and 0<=k_n-n<=b, where b is a fixed nonnegative integer. Then every admissible clock must sample the pulse by index

    N=(L-1)(b+1).

Proof: the N+1 distinct sampled integers k_0,...,k_N lie in [0,N+b]. Since N+b+1=L(b+1), this interval contains exactly b+1 pulse integers and exactly N nonpulse integers. N+1 distinct samples cannot all be nonpulse. This establishes the result uniformly for all b and L, without a finite-scale inference.

The deadline is sharp. Define

    k_n=n+min(floor(n/(L-1)),b).

This clock has increments 1 or2 and obeys the bound for every n. Before N, write n=(L-1)r+s with 0<=s<=L-2 and r<=b. Then k_n=Lr+s, which is not a pulse. At N the cap is b and k_N=Lb+L-1, a pulse. Therefore no universally earlier deadline is possible.

For the inherited L=12 BRC law, first-guaranteed sample index is 11(b+1). Counting the initial n=0 reading, the required worst-case number is 11(b+1)+1: b=0 gives12 readings; b=1 gives23; b=2 gives34. These are detection guarantees for this pulse/comparator pair, not a complete reconstruction guarantee for arbitrary twelve-coordinate ensembles.

The difference between A1 and A2 is whether the clock may repeatedly compensate a skipped pulse by holding the next round. A strict clock has nondecreasing drift k_n-n and can spend its finite skip budget only finitely often. Bounded skew alone does not impose that property.

### A3. Actual reuse, evidence and remaining scope

T0_BRC: REUSE_APPLIED to the precise positive-family/phase observer law above. Branch weights, joint phase and fixed-Q provenance remain in the input source. No positive weights are canceled or replaced by Boolean support. A1/A2 extend its observer lease; they do not extend the world propagation law.

T8_RELATION_OBSERVABLE_SPECTRUM: REUSE_EXECUTED for finite clock-avoidance support only. The unchanged source function src/enterprise_math/relation_future_powerset.py:relation_support_image was executed with its unchanged dependency admissible_support.py, both fetched at the scientific source SHA. At sample n the support stores possible skip counts c. The transition retains b->c precisely when c>=b and (n+c) modL is not L-1. This quotient has a declared support-only clock query; it is not used to merge weighted BRC worlds, phases or path histories. No new general toolbox is proposed.

Executed checker: check_clock_observer.py, 67,143 assertions passed. Complete finite support enumeration covers L=2..24 and b=0..20; every avoidance frontier is nonempty through N-1 and empty at N. It also checks the sharp clock and1201 samples of the bounded-skew hold witness. CLOCK_OBSERVER_VALIDATION.json records exact scope. The all-n proofs establish uniform claims; these checks are supporting finite evidence.

Not executed: original 384-atom BRC suite, independent replication, Lean formalization, sourced physical clock law, or measurement-backreaction experiment. No classical pi, trigonometry, propagator or higher-precision world computation was used.

Next scientific question: use a source-justified incident clock/read protocol to decide whether repeated samples are allowed and whether a finite cumulative skip bound exists. Then derive the complete passive observation quotient for that protocol. Do not repeat the inherited period/pulse calculation or treat A2 as general ensemble identification.

The retained J1 map is Lambda_s(a)=-(u+alpha/u), u=sa and alpha=s/2. This mapping is consumed from the dispatch frontier, not newly proved here. For odd q and alpha!=0 the target image count is (q+eta(alpha))/2, with eta the quadratic character. This turn searches the exact external statement, not the accepted project's proof.

Primary source1: Antonia W. Bluher, arXiv:1707.06877v3, 1 May2021, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1707.06877. Section2, equation(10), Lemma2.1, equations(15)-(16), and Proposition4.1 give the u+1/u fiber and split-image cardinality. The square-alpha case is a direct scaling consequence. This source alone does not literally state the full nonsquare-alpha target. Classification: PARTIAL_ANTECEDENT with explicit domain distinction from D_n(F_q).

Primary source2: Rational functions of degree two or three that are many-to-one on the projective line, DOI https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ffa.2026.102901, publisher article https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1071579726001127. Direct HTML access returned403; the publisher's indexed full Section3 theorem/proof was retrieved by search, and should be rechecked against full authoritative bytes before formal audit acceptance.

Theorem3.1 treats g(x)=(ax^2+bx+c)/(dx+e), ad!=0 and A=a^2e^2+acd^2-abde!=0. For odd q it separates the nonsquare-A two-to-one projective case from the square-A case with two exceptional fibers. Its proof and Theorem3.3 specifically handle x+alpha/x. This is a substantially closer antecedent than a general Dickson value-set paper.

Scope translation, explicitly our inference: choose (a,b,c,d,e)=(1,0,alpha,1,0), so A=alpha. For J_alpha, 0 and infinity both map to infinity, and no nonzero finite x does. Hence removing that one image converts the projective counts (q+1)/2 for nonsquare alpha and (q+3)/2 for square alpha into (q-1)/2 and (q+1)/2, respectively: exactly (q+eta(alpha))/2. Minus sign and u=sa are bijective relabelings. This is a short boundary-removal consequence of the sourced theorem, not a reproof of accepted J1.

Classification: STRONG_PROJECTIVE_ANTECEDENT / EXACT_FINITE_STAR_CONSEQUENCE, pending full-source verification. Do not record the finite-star formula as a verbatim quotation from that paper.
